non_negotiable.title: Update the Payntra README to reflect the real SMTP/MTU root cause — yesterday's non-negotiable still on the board
non_negotiable.reason: The current README documents the SMTP blocker as 'outbound TLS handshake to mail.cyberslide.net:465/587 times out from dev VPS IP — use Resend/Postmark/SES' — but that's wrong. The real root cause was three-headed: (1) Docker bridge MTU 1500 fragmented TLS handshakes against host MTU 1400, (2) env_file: .env wasn't mounted into the app container so SMTP creds were empty, (3) db service wasn't on the same payntra-net as the app so the host `db` didn't resolve. ALL three are fixed in docker-compose.yml. If the next person (you in 3 months, or me on a re-invite) hits a 'SMTP not working' edge case, they'll re-investigate the wrong hypothesis for hours — same as the Jul 5 402-message session did. Payntra is the first real project on the new VPS pipeline, and the README is the only durable record of WHY the deploy was set up the way it is. Yesterday's non-negotiable didn't ship — if you skipped it yesterday, don't skip it again. The compounding cleanup pays off for months.
non_negotiable.action: Open /root/projects/payntra/README.md (or /root/.hermes/projects/payntra if there's a local mirror). Find the 'SMTP Blocker' or 'Outbound Email' section. Replace the 'cloud VPS IP blocked, swap to Resend/Postmark/SES' guidance with the actual fix: (1) Docker bridge MTU forced to 1400 via driver_opts: com.docker.network.driver.mtu: '1400' in the payntra-net network, (2) env_file: .env mounted on BOTH app and db services, (3) db service attached to payntra-net so the `db` host resolves. Include the verification commands: docker exec payntra-app node -e 'nodemailer.createTransport(...).verify()' and curl -X POST https://payntra.terrybot.top/api/auth/forgot-password. Also re-run the Playwright e2e suite (npx playwright test) against the live build to confirm the SMTP/MTU fixes didn't regress anything that was passing before. 20 minutes of work, gates all future Payntra debugging from going down the wrong path again.
